鉴于这一使命，工部局一方面制定了各项有效措施以确保国际租界的安全，另一方面则镇压了一切可能危及当地和平与秩序的活动。因此，在过去的所有内战中，华人不得在租界内从事任何运动。董事会采取此类行动，是因为它不希望租界被用作执行“特殊活动”的“特殊基地”，从而危及当地的和平与秩序。
诚然，城市的繁荣完全归功于董事会的努力，但不应忽视的是，正是中国人对这种繁荣贡献了最大的份额。出于这个原因，租界与中国人民之间的关系如同“身体与灵魂”般紧密。因此，我们非常感谢董事会对国际租界内中国居民的安全和权利的关切。

出于对外侨利益的考虑，中国人将上海部分地区的控制权委托给工部局。后来，租界当局将司法权移交给中国政府。中国政府保证不干涉外侨的合法权利，而租界当局则承诺保护租界内的中国居民。
目前，中日战事已转移至西部战区。虹口曾被日军用作作战基地，现已恢复正常，因此没有必要增加董事会的日籍雇员数量。我们相信，董事会将审视局势的各个方面，并尽力保护中国居民的特权及其安全。
尽管中日之间正在进行战斗，但两国并未宣战，外交关系仍在继续。即使宣战，租界当局作为一个中立机构，也应保护其控制区域内居住的民众。由于尚未宣战，工部局有责任禁止一切可能危及中国居民生命或其权利的活动。
租界内的中国居民开展爱国运动是自然之事。既然日方未表现出任何干涉此类爱国运动的意愿，只要这些运动以合法方式进行，工部局就没有义务对其加以限制。中国人不能忘记自己作为中国公民的身份，正如工部局不能因其 neutrality（中立）地位而忘记自身立场一样。中立并不意味着当局应任意屈从于任何方面的要求；中立意味着维持

董事会忠实地履行了其沉重的责任；它没有忘记中国人对租界繁荣所作的贡献。它在当前中日敌对行动中的中立立场，留下了永远良好的印象。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI'S CURRENT
PROBLEMS

Contrasting strangely with the clear serene autumn day, Shanghai yesterday was in the throes of puzzled thought regarding a whole range of problems which now confront us, following the defeat and retirement of the Chinese forces. With the exception of a mixed force of men now surrounded and holding out in the environs of Nantao there has been a complete withdrawal, and it can be a matter of but a short while before the Japanese military liquidate this last remaining vestige of the opposition in the Shanghai area against which they have waged war for the past three months. There is no practical purpose to be served by this staging of another "Lone Battalion" episode, and one can be pardoned for questioning the decision of certain military and police commanders who have ordered a stand "until the last bullet and the last drop of blood." Prodigality of man-power does not win a war and the sacrifice of many brave men, while it might have a certain moral value to others, is a proceeding against which humanitarian instincts protest. It would have been far better for these men to have made their retreat with the others, to have accompanied those who will eventually reorganize to fight where fighting might be of some military value. The Nantao "last stand" must not only end in the defeat of those who are staging it but it also endangers non-combatant areas which are so urgently needed for the housing of refugees. One does not seek to detract from the valour of the men concerned, but only to question the wisdom of those by whose orders another costly hazard has been created, entailing as it does the lives of men who have earned well of their fellow-countrymen.

But it is not on this point that puzzled thought is now mainly evoked. On all sides many important questions are being asked and giving rise to complex considerations. Certain it is that the former status of much of Shanghai must come under revision. It will possibly be countered that many matters must await the final outcome of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in general, but it has to be conceded that what Shanghai must have as soon as possible is a working settlement of some of the urgent questions of day-to-day administration so that we can get along with a minimum of chaos, dislocation and friction. This journal does not pretend to be able to give answer to a great many of the questions involved, but indication of some of them might serve a public purpose. It has been suggested that the Japanese will ask for greater representation on the Shanghai Municipal Council, that they will ask for the creation of a Japanese Concession in the northern district and that, in any event, they will insist upon the creation of a large and strictly controlled demilitarized zone to prevent any possible recurrence of the present tragedy. The City Government of Greater Shanghai becomes, in the circumstances obtaining to-day, virtually non est in its erstwhile form, and the problem of forming an administrative body later to function in Chinese areas

has to be faced. The setting up of a Peace Preservation Committee will have to be undertaken, and inasmuch as this will be an essential requirement it is to be hoped that any Chinese leaders who might see fit to co-operate in this matter will be spared the charge of being "puppets." Chinese of the type who will be wanted are doubtless now living in the Settlement or Concession, and to them protection will have to be given. Anti-Japanese propaganda within the foreign-controlled areas will have to die down, and the delicate matter of dealing with Chinese censorship over cables, radiograms and the Post Office will have to be faced. It is not to be expected that the Japanese will forego all such fruits of their military gains, and something will possibly be done regarding the functioning and local revenues of the Maritime Customs. We have heard the suggestion made that all such revenues—upon whatever scale they might be—might be credited to a special fund, at least ad interim, but here again clarification of the general situation must be awaited. Regarding the reopening of Chapei, Hongkew, Yangtzepoo, Nantao and the western district it is obvious that special precautions will have to be taken. It would be impossible to allow Chinese freely to re-enter under present conditions, and the Japanese will doubtless ask for their own well-protected re-entry into Settlement areas south of the Soochow Creek so that they may resume their businesses. Political complexities as well as factual difficulties abound here to-day because of the extraordinary position in which the International Settlement now finds itself, and it is going to call for the greatest of patience, forbearance and statesmanship if these problems are to be resolved in other than acrimonious atmosphere.

It was a Chinese decision which led to Shanghai being made the venue of terribly destructive and cruel hostilities, but in the light of the Japanese victory here there must be an accommodation of thought to suit. Well over three-and-a-half million people—many of them destitute—are herded within narrow confines, there is the problem of adequate and cheap food supplies, there is the menace to health, the strict necessity for the maintenance of public law and good order. Surely, no other city has been called upon to face a situation quite comparable to that in which we are now living. Armed forces of several powers have kept inviolate a zone around which major warfare has been waged, both of the combatants being partners in the Settlement itself and one of them having the right to its own armed forces taking part in defence measures. China's sovereignty impinges here in a dozen different ways upon the powers of the local Administration, and now that Japanese forces have created a de facto situation of which Japan will ask note to be taken and for adjustments to suit there is need for a sane, co-operative, realistic view to be shown. Nothing need be feared, we think, by any Chinese living within the Settlement or Concession provided there is studious avoidance of words and deeds
pages.zh:
上海当前的难题

与晴朗宁静的秋日形成奇特反差的是，上海昨日正陷入困惑的沉思之中，思索着在中国军队战败撤退后摆在我们面前的一系列问题。除了一支混合部队目前被包围并在南市周边地区坚持抵抗外，其余部队已全部撤离。日军在过去三个月里对上海地区发动了战争，要清除这最后一点反对势力的残余，恐怕只是时间早晚的问题。再上演一出“孤军”插曲并无实际意义，人们不禁要质疑某些军事和警察指挥官下令“战斗到最后一颗子弹、最后一滴血”的决定是否明智。浪费人力并不能赢得战争，许多勇敢者的牺牲虽然可能对他人具有某种道德价值，但这种做法违背了人道主义本能。这些人最好能随其他部队一起撤退，伴随那些最终将重新集结、在具有军事价值的地方继续作战的人同行。南市的“背水一战”不仅会导致策划者战败，还会危急需用于安置难民的非战斗区域。我们无意贬低相关人员的英勇，只是想质疑那些下令制造另一场代价高昂的冒险行动者的智慧，因为这牵涉到那些为国建功之人的性命。

但目前的困惑主要并非由此引起。各方提出了许多重要问题，引发了复杂的考量。可以肯定的是，上海大部分地区的原有地位必须加以修订。或许有人反驳说，许多事项必须等待中日敌对行动的最终结果，但必须承认，上海当务之急是尽快就日常行政中的一些紧迫问题达成可行的解决方案，以便我们将混乱、脱节和摩擦降至最低。本刊并不声称能回答所涉及的诸多问题，但指出其中一些问题或许能起到服务公众的作用。有人提出，日本方面将要求在工部局董事会中获得更多代表权，要求在北區设立日本租界，并且无论如何都将坚持建立一个大型且受严格控制的非军事区，以防止当前悲剧重演。鉴于目前的局势，大上海市政府在其原有形式上已 virtually（实际上）不复存在，必须面对日后在华人区域组建行政机构的问题。

必须着手成立治安维持委员会，既然这是基本要求，我们希望任何愿意在此事上合作的中国领袖都能免于被指责为“傀儡”。所需类型的中国人无疑正居住在租界或法租界内，必须向他们提供保护。外国控制区域内的反日宣传必须平息，还必须面对处理中国方面对电报、无线电报和邮政审查这一微妙问题。指望日本放弃其军事胜利的所有成果是不现实的，关于海关的运作和地方收入可能会采取某些措施。我们听到有人建议，所有这些收入——无论规模如何——至少暂时记入一个特别基金，但在此问题上仍需等待总体局势的澄清。关于重新开放闸北、虹口、杨树浦、南市和西区，显然必须采取特别预防措施。在目前条件下，不可能允许中国人自由返回，日本方面无疑会要求其受到充分保护地重新进入苏州河以南的租界区域，以便恢复商业活动。由于国际租界目前所处的特殊地位，这里充满了政治复杂性和实际困难，若要非尖刻地解决这些问题，需要极大的耐心、克制和政治家风范。

是中国的决定导致上海成为残酷破坏性战争的战场，但鉴于日本在此获胜，思想必须随之调整以适应局势。超过三百五十万人口——其中许多人贫困潦倒——被挤在狭小的范围内，面临着充足且廉价食品供应的问题、健康威胁，以及维持公共法律和良好秩序的严格必要性。的确，没有其他城市曾像我们现在这样面临如此 comparable（可比拟）的局势。几个国家的武装力量保卫着一个免受侵犯的区域，而重大战争正是在该区域周围进行的，交战双方均为租界本身的伙伴，其中一方有权让其武装部队参与防御措施。中国的主权以十几种不同的方式触及地方行政当局的权力，既然日军造成了既成事实，日本将要求对此予以注意并进行相应调整，因此需要表现出理智、合作和现实的态度。我们认为，只要居住于租界或法租界内的任何中国人谨言慎行，避免发表无视

which fail to take account of changed
conditions. Foreign interests have the
duty of waiting upon actualities and of
trying to aid instead of merely criticizing.
The Japanese authorities must show a
mindfulness for the difficult position in
which merchants and property owners of
all nationalities are with regard to trading
and property interests, and now that
Shanghai has almost wholly passed
through a saddening and destructive
experience to which it ought never have
been so unthinkingly subjected it behoves
all parties and communities to evolve, in
amicable manner, a working formula by
which the process of recovery can be
begun. In a trading way we are bound to
stagnate, more or less, until normal com-
munications with the hinterland are re-
sumed, but in a domestic way we can co-
operate to the end of saving ourselves
avoidable friction and inconvenience. The
predominance of Japanese arms has
changed a great deal, and what we need
is the ability and spirit of adjustment to
that inescapable fact.
pages.zh: 变化局势的言论和行为，就无需恐惧。外国利益方有责任面对现实，并试图提供帮助，而不仅仅是批评。日本当局必须体谅各国商人和业主在贸易和财产利益方面所处的困难境地，既然上海几乎完全经历了一场本不该如此轻率地遭受的令人悲痛和破坏性的磨难，各方和各社区就有责任以友好的方式制定出一种可行的方案，以便开始恢复进程。在贸易方面，在与内地正常交通恢复之前，我们或多或少必将陷入停滞，但在国内事务方面，我们可以合作，以避免不必要的摩擦和不便。日本武力的优势已改变了许多事情，我们需要的是适应这一不可避免事实的能力和态度。
